memory_update.text: MP is the reference public-market anchor for U.S. rare-earth separation and magnet capacity, but it is high-attention and should not crowd out smaller policy-linked processors.

USAR is a priority underfollowed candidate for heavy rare earths, gallium-linked critical minerals, and mine-to-magnet integration; survival depends on milestone-based government funding, financing, and metallurgical/commercial execution.

PPTA is a priority underfollowed antimony candidate because its strategic value is hidden inside a gold-project label; verify antimony trisulfide specifications, permitting, construction financing, and DoD/DLA milestones.
ALM is a tungsten discovery-lane candidate newly relevant to U.S. investors via Nasdaq listing; verify Sangdong commercial ramp, offtake terms, processing economics, and defense qualification.

Graphite, gallium/germanium refiners, rare-earth recyclers, and specialty magnet equipment suppliers remain under-covered in this pass; Westwater Resources and other below-$300M names may require a speculative-shadow micro-cap pass.

node: Critical minerals processing: heavy rare earths, graphite, gallium, germanium, antimony, tungsten, and magnet/refining capacity
summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the critical-minerals-processing node with a two-lane funnel. MP Materials is the obvious U.S.-listed reference anchor for rare-earth separation and magnets. The underfollowed lane contains USA Rare Earth for heavy rare earths/gallium/magnets, Perpetua Resources for antimony trisulfide tied to defense supply chains, and Almonty Industries for tungsten supply and processing capacity. These are research candidates only, not recommendations; the main falsification risks are permitting, metallurgical scale-up, customer qualification, project financing, dilution, and government-funding milestone conditions.
